sample_type.evidence_source: [/page/11/Text/6] As expected, peer victimization on Facebook marginally predicted decreases in adolescents' life satisfaction. These results are consistent with prior studies examining the longitudinal impact of online peer victimization on adolescents' psychosocial well-being (e.g., Sumter et al. 2012). Although this finding was only marginally significant, it suggests that victimized youth might interpret negative peer acts on Facebook as negative peer evaluations.
